children: Shares of luxury electric vehicle maker Lucid fell Monday after it missed analyst expectations both for earnings and revenue. But traders may have been more concerned by another detail in the report: it announced a $1.75 billion delayed-draw term loan from Saudi Arabia's sovereign-wealth fund.

While the loan should help the car maker as it prepares to launch its sub-$50,000 Cosmos midsize crossover sports utility vehicle next year, it raises concerns about the Lucid's burgeoning debt. It now has more than $4 billion in combined short- and long-term debt as well as $931 million in cash and cash equivalents.

The Newark, Calif.-based EV maker has been heavily reliant on the Saudis, even before it released its first car, the Lucid Air sedan in 2021. Saudi Arabia's sovereign-wealth fund owns more than 50% of Lucid stock and has already pumped some $9 billion into the car maker, including loans, since 2018, when it invested its first $1 billion to build the company's factory in Casa Grande, Az.

Lucid has also been under pressure as sales of electric vehicles have slowed and tax credits have expired. EV sales have fallen from 10% of all new car sales a year ago to just 6% as of the third quarter this year. Analysts are expecting Lucid to sell just 16,000 vehicles this year, down from the 140,000 once projected back in 2022 shortly after the company went public.

One new initiative taking shape is the company's public launch of its robo-taxi service in the U.S. next year in partnership with Uber and Nuro. It reiterated that the driverless vehicles will launch in the San Francisco Bay Area in the first three months of 2027, something Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi said earlier this month.
A Houston launch is also slated for next year. Lucid also planning a European rollout with partner Bolt, with vehicle deliveries in 2027 or 2028.
